title: Sample project: pricing page redesign (fictional)

first_insight.text: The creator steered this project: they set firm limits, turned down a first design, and chose what to put off.
first_insight.why: Their own messages set the limits and reject the first layout, and their notes say what to put off.

findings.text: Before any work began, the creator said what the page had to do: three price plans, no yearly toggle, and everything visible on one screen.
The creator turned down the first layout as too busy and asked for a plain table. The AI then made a simpler version.
Saved changes to the pricing page were made the same day each draft was discussed. That fits a pattern of reviewing first, then saving.
The creator rewrote the free plan wording after the AI's draft. A later note says the draft promised too much support.
The project notes say billing was put off until the page launches. They give "scope", meaning the size of the job, as the reason.

unknowns: We can't tell whether any decisions were made in meetings or messages that were not shared.
We can't tell who typed each line of code. Saved changes show what changed, not who wrote it.
We can't tell whether a design tool was used, because no design file was shared.

evidence.label: Creator's opening request to Claude
evidence.excerpt: I want three tiers and no annual toggle. The page should load fast and the comparison should fit on one screen.

evidence.label: Creator's message cutting a section
evidence.excerpt: Drop the testimonials section for now. We only need pricing and the comparison.

evidence.label: Creator's feedback on the first layout
evidence.excerpt: This layout is too busy. Make the comparison a plain table and remove the icons.

evidence.label: Saved change: pricing page with three plans
Saved change: cards replaced by a table
Saved change: free plan wording rewritten
evidence.excerpt: Rewrite free tier copy; the draft overpromised support.

evidence.label: Project notes: decisions
evidence.excerpt: Decision: defer billing integration until the page ships. Reason: scope.
